title: Effective Federal Funds Rate

source.name: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)

summary: The Effective Federal Funds Rate stood at 3.64% as of April 8, 2026, unchanged from the prior four days (April 4-8). This daily snapshot reflects the actual rate at which depository institutions lend reserve balances to other depository institutions overnight. No policy change or commentary accompanies this data point.
key_points: Effective Federal Funds Rate: 3.64% as of 2026-04-08
Rate unchanged over five consecutive observations (April 4-8, 2026)
Series code: DFF, sourced from FRED
why_it_matters: The effective federal funds rate is the primary policy instrument of the Federal Reserve, directly influencing short-term borrowing costs across the economy. A stable rate at 3.64% suggests no change in monetary policy stance during this period. This data point serves as a reference for market participants assessing the current cost of short-term capital.
macro_context: The stable 3.64% EFFR reflects an unchanged monetary policy environment. This rate level is used as a benchmark for various short-term instruments and influences funding costs throughout the financial system. Without accompanying policy statements, the macro context is limited to this static reading.
